response: Micheál Martin was in Limerick this past week trying to spin that housing tenancies have gone up, but that distracts from the surge in eviction notices and homelessness that came after the government's March 1 rules forcing landlords to offer six-year leases. Nationally the number of people stuck in emergency accommodation has increased again, exposing how these weak measures fail to protect vulnerable groups from the structural inequalities and landlord power driving the housing crisis. We need urgent, serious reforms to confront the root causes of exploitation and guarantee stable homes as a basic right instead of letting profits dominate—it's time to stop the system from serving the powerful at everyone else's expense.
